title: Turning Toward
logline: At a town three-wheeler stand, a driver's eyes move to every passer-by, and in a fraction of a second, before anyone speaks, he has already decided: customer, or not.
human_question: What is the very first thing a mind does when someone catches its attention, before any decision is made about them?

premise.story: A three-wheeler driver waits at a stand through a working day, watching passers-by, calling out to some, letting most go, and occasionally landing a fare.
premise.place: A town three-wheeler stand on a busy street.
premise.experience: The viewer watches hundreds of small, mostly wasted turns of attention, and starts to notice the tiny, repeated moment where a glance either goes nowhere or becomes an approach.

concept_links.why: The source's turning toward mind points at an object without yet knowing anything about it, and its determining function settles what something is just before any response [C010-P:L29-L37]. A driver's glance at every passer-by is a documentary version of exactly this turning and settling.
The source's account of the fourteen functions of mind as a relay, each step handing on to the next, matches the driver's repeated cycle of noticing, sizing up, and calling out or not.
Effort and decisiveness, the source's occasional mental factors, show up unevenly across a driver's day, sharp when a fare looks likely, absent through long empty stretches.

what_camera_could_observe: The driver's eyes moving over the passing crowd
A call made, and a call withheld
A fare negotiated, or a passer-by who was never really a prospect
The driver's own account of how he reads the street
what_must_be_real: The driver's real economics and working conditions; no staged misses or exaggerated reactions. His own account of his day, not a narrated explanation of his glances.

possible_arc.opening: The stand fills with drivers; the day's watching begins.
possible_arc.turn: A slow day, a difficult fare, or a rival driver tests his patience and judgement.
possible_arc.ending_open: The day ends with whatever the driver actually earned and however he actually feels about it.

position_hint: middle: a small-scale, everyday urban film that gives the group texture beyond craft and nature settings.

requirements: A busy three-wheeler stand with drivers willing to be filmed over a working day
A vantage point that can follow both the driver and the passing street
Consent that respects the driver's livelihood and does not slow his actual work

suggestions.name: A busy stand in a market town
suggestions.region: Any market town, to be selected
suggestions.why: Three-wheeler stands are a near-universal feature of Sri Lankan town life; a specific town is left open.
suggestions.verify: A specific stand and a willing driver are unconfirmed.

risks: Reducing the driver to an illustration of a single mental process rather than a full person
Voice-over or narration that claims to know what he is thinking at each glance
Treating an ordinary livelihood as merely picturesque
drop_if: No driver is willing to be filmed candidly over real working hours
The stand turns out to be too quiet or too chaotic to observe clearly
The film cannot avoid narrating the driver's inner state instead of showing his actions

connections.note: Both are studies of an ordinary working day built from repeated small acts of noticing and response.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
